questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code preserves the order of playback events for a session? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Why does the publisher use event.sessionId() as the record key?
choices: So Kafka compacts the topic down to one event per session.
So all events for one session hash to the same partition, where order is preserved, while different sessions can be processed in parallel.
So the consumer can skip deserializing the value for sessions it does not own.
So every event for a video goes to the same consumer instance.

questions.prompt: In PlaybackStateConsumer, applying the record at offset N of one partition throws. What is the observable result?
choices: The consumer commits past N so the poison event cannot block the group, and logs a warning.
The whole batch is abandoned and no offsets at all are committed for any partition.
The exception propagates out of run() and the consumer closes.
Records after N in that partition from this poll are not applied, offsets up to N-1 are committed, and N is fetched again on the next poll; other partitions continue normally.

questions.prompt: The consumer crashes after SessionProjection.apply for a batch but before commitSync. After restart, what happens to those records?
choices: They are redelivered, and the projection tolerates it because apply ignores events whose seq is not greater than the session's lastSeq.
They are lost, because auto commit is disabled.
They are redelivered and every event is applied a second time, double counting playback.
They are skipped because the group already holds their offsets.
